newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government will dissolve parliament in two years with or without the new constitution. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says. He says he will call a new general election even if the new charter cannot be completed in two years. (BANGKOK POST)

- Burmese troops are poised to seize the Karen National Union's (KNU) jungle headquarters after the Karen rebels burned down and retreated from their camp in the face of overwhelming government forces. Burmese gunners also shelled a Karen refugee camp in a village of Umphang district - which is about six kilometres from the border. The Karen refugees fled to the Thai village just a few days ago, shortly ahead of Burmese attacks on KNU headquarters and two other camps. (BANGKOK POST)

- Police have turned the heat on the Bank of Thailand, blaming its minsinterpretation of the law on the collapse of one of the cases involving the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) scandal, and accusing it of having cooperated poorly with investigators. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says he has instructed Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan to investigate the dubious mistake which allowed key BBC suspects to evade charges under the banking law. (THE NATION)

- Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitpol has escaped being censured by parliament for corrupt and shameful behaviour following a debate. Members of the House voted in favour of the besieged minister who the opposition alleged bribed 122 fellow MPs with 50,000-baht payments. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST) + + + +

- Independent Power (Thailand) is to borrow 5.170 billion baht from five local financial institutions and $176 million from seven foreign financial institutions for the construction of a thermal power station and associated transmission facilities. The Project Financing Facilities Agreement was signed yesterday, at the same time as the first-ever Power Purchase Agreement under the Independent Power Producers scheme for the supply of power to the electricity Generating Authority of Thailand. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Foreign airlines operating into Thailand believe an increase in travel tax will be counter-productive and detrimental in the long-term to both Thai aviation and tourism, says spokesperson for the Board of Airlines. Strong rumours are circulating that Thailand is to impose a 1,500 baht travel tax in March to curb outbound travel and hence reduce the current account deficit. (THE NATION)

- The government has decided to go ahead with the southern landbridge project approved by the previous administration, putting an end to rumours that the route would be changed again. The landbridge will link deep seaports on both sides of the southern peninsula. (BANGKOK POST)
